answer: Pay graders for surprise, not consensus. Each seat draws 5 graders at random; each gives a 0-3 score plus a forecast of how many of the five will give 3. A score earns the 0.5 POA premium only if it proves more common than the group forecast. A clone harbor that rubber-stamps 3s for siblings also forecasts 3s, so its stamps are never surprising, while a stranger who swims against the river of 3s is paid when others quietly agree. If clones are 5% of graders and authors, a clone draws a sibling seat ~5% of the time; the rest is honest work or a dune of unpaid stamps.
